Every property below is one the runtime interprets, and the list is written by the runtime: a property is on this page exactly when the runtime honors it, and is described in the words the editor shows on hover. Anything else is parsed, ignored and reported once on stderr. [Honored CSS](/reference/css/) says how each one behaves in detail, and [where Rux differs from CSS](/reference/css-differences/) lists the places Rux behaves differently and what to write there.

249 properties and 26 pseudo-classes, as of `rux 0.9.0-dev`.

## Properties

| Property | What it does | Keywords | Animates |
|---|---|---|---|
| `display` | **how this box lays its children out.** `block` (the default), `flex`, `grid`, `inline` or `none`. **Rux defaults to `block`**, so a box does not lay its children out in a row until you say `display: flex`. Rux has no inline level for a box, so `inline-flex` is `flex`, `inline-grid` is `grid` and `inline-block` is `block`; a value with no layout here (`contents`, `table`) warns and is `block`.For example `.row { display: flex; }` | `block` `flex` `grid` `inline` `none` `inline-flex` `inline-grid` `inline-block` `flow-root` |  |
| `width` | **how wide the box is.** A length or a percentage of the parent's width. A child of a flex column already fills its width, since the cross-axis default is `stretch`; `width` is for when it should not.For example `.field { width: 100%; }` |  | yes |
| `height` | **how tall the box is.** A length or a percentage. A definite height is half of what makes a scroller; the other half is `overflow`.For example `.thread { height: 300px; }` |  | yes |
| `gap` | **space between children.** On a flex or grid parent. Space *between* items only, never outside them, which is what makes it different from margin.For example `.row { display: flex; gap: 8px; }` |  | yes |
| `min-width` | **a width it will not go under.** Stops a flex item shrinking past this. `min-width: 0` is the escape hatch when an item refuses to shrink at all.For example `.cell { min-width: 0; }` |  |  |
| `max-width` | **a width it will not go over.** Caps the box however much room there is. Common on text so a line does not run the full window.For example `.msg { max-width: 320px; }` |  |  |
| `min-height` | **a height it will not go under.** Useful on a scroller that must keep its size when empty.For example `.panel { min-height: 120px; }` |  |  |
| `max-height` | **a height it will not go over.** Caps growth; pair with `overflow` to scroll the excess rather than clip it.For example `.menu { max-height: 240px; overflow-y: auto; }` |  |  |
| `padding` | **space inside the border, all four sides.** One to four lengths, clockwise from the top. Inside the background, so padding is painted in the box's own colour.For example `.card { padding: 12px 16px; }` |  | yes |
| `padding-top` | **space inside the top edge.** Overrides the `padding` shorthand for this side.For example `.card { padding-top: 12px; }` |  |  |
| `padding-right` | **space inside the right edge.** Overrides the `padding` shorthand for this side.For example `.card { padding-right: 16px; }` |  |  |
| `padding-bottom` | **space inside the bottom edge.** Overrides the `padding` shorthand for this side.For example `.card { padding-bottom: 12px; }` |  |  |
| `padding-left` | **space inside the left edge.** Overrides the `padding` shorthand for this side.For example `.card { padding-left: 16px; }` |  |  |
| `margin` | **space outside the box, all four sides.** One to four lengths, clockwise from the top. Outside the background, so it shows the parent through.For example `.card { margin: 0 auto; }` |  | yes |
| `margin-top` | **space outside the top edge.** Overrides the `margin` shorthand for this side.For example `.card { margin-top: 8px; }` |  |  |
| `margin-right` | **space outside the right edge.** Overrides the `margin` shorthand for this side.For example `.card { margin-right: 8px; }` |  |  |
| `margin-bottom` | **space outside the bottom edge.** Overrides the `margin` shorthand for this side.For example `.card { margin-bottom: 8px; }` |  |  |
| `margin-left` | **space outside the left edge.** Overrides the `margin` shorthand for this side.For example `.card { margin-left: 8px; }` |  |  |
| `border` | **width, style and colour of the outline.** `2px solid #45475a`. The style word is accepted and only the width and colour are drawn.For example `.field { border: 2px solid #45475a; }` |  |  |
| `border-width` | **how thick the outline is.** Takes room in the layout, so changing it moves the content inside.For example `.field { border-width: 2px; }` |  | yes |
| `border-color` | **what colour the outline is.** Animatable, so it is the usual way to show focus without the box moving. One to four colours, top, right, bottom, left, as `margin` takes lengths.For example `.field:focus { border-color: #89b4fa; }` |  | yes |
| `border-top-color` | **the top edge's colour.** Overrides `border-color` for this side. A border whose sides differ in colour is drawn side by side, each with its own; only the box's `border-color` animates.For example `.tab { border-top-color: #89b4fa; }` |  |  |
| `border-right-color` | **the right edge's colour.** Overrides `border-color` for this side.For example `.cell { border-right-color: #313244; }` |  |  |
| `border-bottom-color` | **the bottom edge's colour.** Overrides `border-color` for this side.For example `.row { border-bottom-color: #313244; }` |  |  |
| `border-left-color` | **the left edge's colour.** Overrides `border-color` for this side.For example `.quote { border-left-color: #f9e2af; }` |  |  |
| `border-radius` | **how round the corners are.** One to four lengths, grouped by diagonal. Takes a percentage, resolved against the box's shorter side, so `50%` rounds a square into a circle and an oblong into a pill. Clips the background and the border; it does **not** clip children unless the box also has `overflow: hidden`.For example `.card { border-radius: 12px; }` |  | yes |
| `border-top-left-radius` | **roundness of one corner.** Overrides `border-radius` for this corner.For example `.bubble { border-top-left-radius: 2px; }` |  |  |
| `border-top-right-radius` | **roundness of one corner.** Overrides `border-radius` for this corner.For example `.bubble { border-top-right-radius: 2px; }` |  |  |
| `border-bottom-right-radius` | **roundness of one corner.** Overrides `border-radius` for this corner.For example `.bubble { border-bottom-right-radius: 2px; }` |  |  |
| `border-bottom-left-radius` | **roundness of one corner.** Overrides `border-radius` for this corner.For example `.bubble { border-bottom-left-radius: 2px; }` |  |  |
| `border-top` | **the top edge's width and colour.** The one-side form of the `border` shorthand.For example `.footer { border-top: 1px solid #313244; }` |  |  |
| `border-right` | **the right edge's width and colour.** The one-side form of the `border` shorthand.For example `.sidebar { border-right: 1px solid #313244; }` |  |  |
| `border-bottom` | **the bottom edge's width and colour.** The one-side form of the `border` shorthand. A cheap way to draw a divider under a row.For example `.row { border-bottom: 1px solid #313244; }` |  |  |
| `border-left` | **the left edge's width and colour.** The one-side form of the `border` shorthand. A cheap way to draw a quote bar.For example `.quote { border-left: 3px solid #89b4fa; }` |  |  |
| `border-top-width` | **thickness of the top edge.** Set on its own, leaving the colour to the shorthand.For example `.row { border-top-width: 1px; }` |  |  |
| `border-right-width` | **thickness of the right edge.** Set on its own, leaving the colour to the shorthand.For example `.row { border-right-width: 1px; }` |  |  |
| `border-bottom-width` | **thickness of the bottom edge.** Set on its own, leaving the colour to the shorthand.For example `.row { border-bottom-width: 1px; }` |  |  |
| `border-left-width` | **thickness of the left edge.** Set on its own, leaving the colour to the shorthand.For example `.row { border-left-width: 3px; }` |  |  |
| `overflow` | **what happens to content too big for the box.** `auto` or `scroll` makes this box **the scroller**; `hidden` or `clip` cuts the overflow off. **Nothing in Rux scrolls until a box is told to**, and the box told is the one with a definite size.For example `.thread { height: 300px; overflow: auto; }` | `visible` `hidden` `clip` `auto` `scroll` |  |
| `overflow-x` | **the same, for the horizontal axis only.** Use when a row should scroll sideways while the page does not.For example `.tabs { overflow-x: auto; }` | `visible` `hidden` `clip` `auto` `scroll` |  |
| `overflow-y` | **the same, for the vertical axis only.** The usual half: a list that scrolls while the screen around it stays put.For example `.thread { height: 300px; overflow-y: auto; }` | `visible` `hidden` `clip` `auto` `scroll` |  |
| `overscroll-behavior` | **whether scrolling past the end passes outward.** `auto` (the default) lets what this scroller cannot take go on to the scroller around it, so a list at its end lets the page scroll. `contain` or `none` keeps it here. One value for both axes, or `x y`.For example `.sheet .list { overscroll-behavior: contain; }` | `auto` `contain` `none` |  |
| `overscroll-behavior-x` | **the same, sideways only.** `auto`, `contain` or `none`, for the horizontal axis.For example `.carousel { overscroll-behavior-x: contain; }` | `auto` `contain` `none` |  |
| `overscroll-behavior-y` | **the same, up and down only.** `auto`, `contain` or `none`, for the vertical axis: a panel whose list should never scroll the page behind it.For example `.panel { overscroll-behavior-y: contain; }` | `auto` `contain` `none` |  |
| `scrollbar-width` | **how thick the scrollbars are drawn.** `auto`, `thin`, or `none`, which draws no bar while the box still scrolls. Bars show while the box scrolls or the pointer is over it, then fade.For example `.tabs { scrollbar-width: none; }` | `auto` `thin` `none` |  |
| `scrollbar-color` | **the scrollbars' thumb and track colours.** Two colours, thumb then track, or `auto` for the default grey.For example `.thread { scrollbar-color: #89b4fa transparent; }` | `auto` |  |
| `clip-path` | **cut the box to a shape.** `circle()`, `ellipse()`, `inset(… round …)`, `polygon()`, `path()`, `xywh()` or `rect()`, over `border-box` (the default), `padding-box`, `content-box` or `margin-box`. The box and everything in it are cut; taps are not yet.For example `.avatar { clip-path: circle(50%); }` |  |  |
| `mask-image` | **show the box only where an image or gradient is.** A gradient or `url()`, laid over the border box: the box and everything in it show where the mask is opaque, and fade where it fades. `mask-mode: luminance` uses how light it is instead. An image covers the box, as `background-image` does.For example `.fade { mask-image: linear-gradient(black, transparent); }` |  |  |
| `mask` | **mask-image and mask-mode at once.** `mask: linear-gradient(black, transparent)`, and `luminance` to mask by lightness.For example `.fade { mask: linear-gradient(to right, black 80%, transparent); }` |  |  |
| `mask-mode` | **mask by opacity or by lightness.** `alpha` (and `match-source`, the default) or `luminance`.For example `.logo { mask-mode: luminance; }` | `alpha` `luminance` `match-source` |  |
| `border-style` | **how the border's line is drawn.** `solid`, `dashed`, `dotted`, `double`, `groove`, `ridge`, `inset`, `outset`, `hidden` or `none`, one to four values like `margin`. **A border with no style draws nothing**, as in CSS: write `border: 2px solid red`, not `border: 2px red`.For example `.drop-zone { border-width: 2px; border-style: dashed; }` | `solid` `dashed` `dotted` `double` `groove` `ridge` `inset` `outset` `hidden` `none` |  |
| `border-top-style` | **how the top edge is drawn.** One of the `border-style` values, for that side alone.For example `.row { border-top-style: dotted; }` |  |  |
| `border-right-style` | **how the right edge is drawn.** One of the `border-style` values, for that side alone.For example `.row { border-right-style: dotted; }` |  |  |
| `border-bottom-style` | **how the bottom edge is drawn.** One of the `border-style` values, for that side alone.For example `.row { border-bottom-style: dotted; }` |  |  |
| `border-left-style` | **how the left edge is drawn.** One of the `border-style` values, for that side alone.For example `.row { border-left-style: dotted; }` |  |  |
| `text-shadow` | **a shadow or glow under the text.** `x y blur colour`, and a comma list of them, the first on top. Inherited. With no colour it is the text's own: `text-shadow: 0 0 8px` glows in the text colour.For example `.title { text-shadow: 0 1px 2px #00000066; }` |  |  |
| `filter` | **blur or recolour the box and everything in it.** `blur()`, `brightness()`, `contrast()`, `drop-shadow()`, `grayscale()`, `hue-rotate()`, `invert()`, `opacity()`, `saturate()` and `sepia()`, applied in the order written.For example `.disabled { filter: grayscale(1) opacity(0.6); }` |  | yes |
| `backdrop-filter` | **blur or recolour what is behind the box.** The same functions as `filter`, applied to what is drawn behind the box and shown inside it: `backdrop-filter: blur(12px)` is frosted glass. | `mix-blend-mode` | **how the box blends with what is under it.** `multiply`, `screen`, `overlay`, `darken`, `lighten`, `color-dodge`, `color-burn`, `hard-light`, `soft-light`, `difference`, `exclusion`, `hue`, `saturation`, `color` or `luminosity`. The box and everything in it blend as one layer.For example `.stamp { mix-blend-mode: multiply; }` | `normal` `multiply` `screen` `overlay` `darken` `lighten` `color-dodge` `color-burn` `hard-light` `soft-light` `difference` `exclusion` `hue` `saturation` `color` `luminosity` |  |
| `opacity` | **how see-through the whole box is.** `0` to `1`, and it applies to the **subtree**, not just this box. Animatable, and the cheapest thing to animate.For example `.msg:enter-from { opacity: 0; }` |  | yes |
| `cursor` | **the pointer shape over this box.** Every CSS keyword, on any box, inherited. `url()` images are skipped for the keyword after them. Applied by the shell on hover.For example `.send { cursor: pointer; }` | `auto` `default` `none` `context-menu` `help` `pointer` `progress` `wait` `cell` `crosshair` `text` `vertical-text` `alias` `copy` `move` `no-drop` `not-allowed` `grab` `grabbing` `all-scroll` `col-resize` `row-resize` `n-resize` `e-resize` `s-resize` `w-resize` `ne-resize` `nw-resize` `se-resize` `sw-resize` `ew-resize` `ns-resize` `nesw-resize` `nwse-resize` `zoom-in` `zoom-out` |  |
| `touch-action` | **which axes a finger may still scroll here.** Decides who wins when a `@drag` and a scroller want the same finger. The default `auto` lets the scroller keep any axis it can actually scroll, so a drag inside a scrolling list does not trap the page; `none` gives the element the finger outright; `pan-x` and `pan-y` keep one axis for the scroller. Settled once, when the finger passes the drag threshold. Touch only: a mouse scrolls by wheel, not by dragging.For example `.slider { touch-action: none; }` | `auto` `none` `pan-x` `pan-y` `manipulation` |  |
| `box-shadow` | **a shadow cast by the box.** `x y blur spread colour`, and a comma list of them, the first on top. | `outline` | **a line around the box, outside its border.** `width style colour`, in any order. Takes no space, is drawn over the element's content, and follows `border-radius`. | `outline-width` | **the outline's thickness.** A length, or `thin`, `medium` (the initial, 3px) or `thick`. `0` removes the outline.For example `.send { outline-width: 3px; }` |  |  |
| `transform` | **move, rotate or scale the painted box.** `translate`, `rotate`, `scale`, composed left to right. Paint-only, so it never moves anything else. **A transformed box becomes the containing block** for `absolute` *and* `fixed` descendants, which is why a `fixed` child stops being fixed inside one.For example `.msg:enter-from { transform: translateY(10px); }` |  | yes |

| `transition-duration` | **how long each transition takes.** A comma list of times, repeated to the length of `transition-property`.For example `.btn { transition-duration: 150ms; }` |  |  |

| `transition-delay` | **how long each transition waits.** A comma list of times, repeated to the length of `transition-property`.For example `.btn { transition-delay: 50ms; }` |  |  |

| `font-variant` | **small capitals, numerals and ligatures.** Any of the `font-variant-*` keywords; the font's own OpenType features.For example `.heading { font-variant: small-caps; }` | `normal` `none` `small-caps` `all-small-caps` `tabular-nums` `oldstyle-nums` `slashed-zero` |  |
| `font-variant-caps` | **small capitals.** `small-caps`, `all-small-caps`, `petite-caps` and the rest, when the font has them.For example `.heading { font-variant-caps: all-small-caps; }` | `normal` `small-caps` `all-small-caps` `petite-caps` `all-petite-caps` `unicase` `titling-caps` |  |
| `font-variant-numeric` | **how numerals are drawn.** `tabular-nums` for columns that line up, `oldstyle-nums`, fractions, `ordinal`, `slashed-zero`.For example `.price { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }` | `normal` `lining-nums` `oldstyle-nums` `proportional-nums` `tabular-nums` `diagonal-fractions` `stacked-fractions` `ordinal` `slashed-zero` |  |
| `font-variant-ligatures` | **which ligatures the font joins.** `none`, `no-common-ligatures`, `discretionary-ligatures` and the rest.For example `.code { font-variant-ligatures: none; }` | `normal` `none` `common-ligatures` `no-common-ligatures` `discretionary-ligatures` `no-discretionary-ligatures` `historical-ligatures` `no-historical-ligatures` `contextual` `no-contextual` |  |
| `font-variant-position` | **the font's own subscripts and superscripts.** `sub` or `super`, when the font has them.For example `.note { font-variant-position: super; }` | `normal` `sub` `super` |  |
| `font-variant-east-asian` | **East Asian glyph forms.** `jis78` to `jis04`, `simplified`, `traditional`, `full-width`, `proportional-width`, `ruby`.For example `.jp { font-variant-east-asian: jis04; }` | `normal` `jis78` `jis83` `jis90` `jis04` `simplified` `traditional` `full-width` `proportional-width` `ruby` |  |
| `font-feature-settings` | **OpenType features by tag.** `"tnum"`, `"liga" 0`: drawn after `font-variant`, so it wins where they meet.For example `.price { font-feature-settings: "tnum"; }` |  |  |
| `font-variation-settings` | **a variable font's axes by tag.** `"wght" 650, "wdth" 80`.For example `.title { font-variation-settings: "wght" 650; }` |  |  |
| `font-stretch` | **a narrower or wider face.** `condensed` to `expanded`, or a percentage, from the font's width axis or its narrow and wide faces.For example `.dense { font-stretch: condensed; }` | `normal` `ultra-condensed` `extra-condensed` `condensed` `semi-condensed` `semi-expanded` `expanded` `extra-expanded` `ultra-expanded` |  |
| `font-width` | **the newer name of `font-stretch`.** The same values.For example `.dense { font-width: 75%; }` | `normal` `condensed` `expanded` |  |
| `caret-color` | **the colour of a field's caret.** `auto` is the text's colour. Inherited.For example `.field { caret-color: #f38ba8; }` | `auto` |  |
| `object-fit` | **how an image fills its box.** `fill` (stretched, the default), `contain`, `cover`, `none` or `scale-down`.For example `.avatar { object-fit: cover; }` | `fill` `contain` `cover` `none` `scale-down` |  |
| `object-position` | **where an image sits in its box.** One to four values, as `background-position`: `left`, `right 8px bottom 8px`.For example `.avatar { object-position: top; }` | `center` `top` `right` `bottom` `left` |  |
| `pointer-events` | **whether a pointer can reach the box.** `none` lets a tap through to what is under it; the keyboard still reaches it. Inherited.For example `.glass { pointer-events: none; }` | `auto` `none` |  |
| `scroll-behavior` | **whether a scroll asked for glides.** `smooth` on a scroller: `scrollIntoView()` and Tab glide there. A wheel or a finger never does.For example `.list { scroll-behavior: smooth; }` | `auto` `smooth` |  |
| `scroll-snap-type` | **where a scroller comes to rest.** On a scroller: `x`, `y` or `both`, then `mandatory` (always rests on a snap point) or `proximity` (only when one is near, the default). A wheel, a finger, a fling and `scrollIntoView()` all come to rest on one.For example `.pages { scroll-snap-type: x mandatory; }` | `none` `x mandatory` `y mandatory` `both mandatory` `x proximity` `y proximity` |  |
| `scroll-snap-align` | **where a box meets its scroller's view.** On a box in a snapping scroller: `start`, `center` or `end`, one value for both axes or block then inline. The scroller can rest with that edge of the box at the same edge of its view.For example `.page { scroll-snap-align: center; }` | `none` `start` `center` `end` |  |
| `scroll-snap-stop` | **whether a fling may pass this box.** `always`: a fling stops here rather than passing by, as a carousel's pages do. `normal` lets it pass.For example `.page { scroll-snap-stop: always; }` | `normal` `always` |  |
| `scroll-padding` | **insets a snapping scroller's view.** One to four lengths or percentages of the view, clockwise from the top: where the boxes snap to, under a sticky header for one.For example `.list { scroll-padding: 48px 0 0; }` |  |  |
| `scroll-padding-top` | **insets the top of a snapping view.** Overrides the `scroll-padding` shorthand for this side.For example `.list { scroll-padding-top: 48px; }` |  |  |
| `scroll-padding-right` | **insets the right of a snapping view.** Overrides the `scroll-padding` shorthand for this side.For example `.list { scroll-padding-right: 16px; }` |  |  |
| `scroll-padding-bottom` | **insets the bottom of a snapping view.** Overrides the `scroll-padding` shorthand for this side.For example `.list { scroll-padding-bottom: 16px; }` |  |  |
| `scroll-padding-left` | **insets the left of a snapping view.** Overrides the `scroll-padding` shorthand for this side.For example `.list { scroll-padding-left: 16px; }` |  |  |
| `scroll-margin` | **grows a box for snapping.** One to four lengths, clockwise from the top, added around the box where it snaps, and nowhere else.For example `.row { scroll-margin: 8px; }` |  |  |
| `scroll-margin-top` | **grows a box's top for snapping.** Overrides the `scroll-margin` shorthand for this side.For example `.row { scroll-margin-top: 8px; }` |  |  |
| `scroll-margin-right` | **grows a box's right for snapping.** Overrides the `scroll-margin` shorthand for this side.For example `.row { scroll-margin-right: 8px; }` |  |  |
| `scroll-margin-bottom` | **grows a box's bottom for snapping.** Overrides the `scroll-margin` shorthand for this side.For example `.row { scroll-margin-bottom: 8px; }` |  |  |
| `scroll-margin-left` | **grows a box's left for snapping.** Overrides the `scroll-margin` shorthand for this side.For example `.row { scroll-margin-left: 8px; }` |  |  |
| `overflow-wrap` | **whether a long word may break mid-word.** `break-word` or `anywhere` let an unbreakable word break rather than overflow.For example `.body { overflow-wrap: break-word; }` | `normal` `break-word` `anywhere` |  |
| `word-wrap` | **the older name for `overflow-wrap`.** Accepted as a synonym.For example `.body { word-wrap: break-word; }` | `normal` `break-word` `anywhere` |  |
| `word-break` | **how aggressively words break.** `break-all` breaks anywhere at all, not only to avoid an overflow.For example `.code { word-break: break-all; }` | `normal` `break-all` |  |
| `fill` | **the colour inside the path.** On `<path>`. Paint is CSS here rather than an SVG attribute, which is what gives a path `:hover`, `:class` and `transition`. Animatable.For example `.mark { fill: #f9e2af; }` |  | yes |
| `fill-rule` | **which parts count as inside.** `nonzero` (the default) or `evenodd`. The difference shows on a shape that crosses itself, like a star.For example `.star { fill-rule: evenodd; }` | `nonzero` `evenodd` |  |
| `stroke` | **the colour of the outline.** On `<path>`. Animatable.For example `.mark { stroke: #1e1e2e; }` |  | yes |
| `stroke-width` | **how thick the outline is.** On `<path>`. Animatable, so a line can thicken on hover.For example `.mark { stroke-width: 2; }` |  | yes |
| `stroke-linecap` | **the shape of a line's ends.** `butt` (the default), `round` or `square`.For example `.mark { stroke-linecap: round; }` | `butt` `round` `square` |  |
| `stroke-linejoin` | **the shape where two segments meet.** `miter` (the default), `round` or `bevel`.For example `.mark { stroke-linejoin: round; }` | `miter` `round` `bevel` |  |

## Pseudo-classes

| Pseudo-class | What it matches |
|---|---|
| `:hover` | **the pointer is over this box.** Needs a layout region, so the shell can tell when the pointer enters and leaves it. There is no hover on a touch screen, so it can decorate and must not be the only way to reach something. |
| `:focus` | **this element has the keyboard.** A field, a select or a `@tap` box, reached by tapping it or by walking the focus order with Tab. The element itself only, not its ancestors. For the ring, prefer `:focus-visible`, which leaves a tapped button alone. |
| `:focus-visible` | **focused, and it should show.** A field whenever it has focus; anything else only when the keyboard put focus there, so a button tapped with a finger shows nothing and the same button reached with Tab does. The default ring is this rule's `outline: auto`, so `outline: none` here removes it and any other `outline` replaces it. |
| `:active` | **a press is down on this box.** Held between press and release, so it is the state a button uses to look pushed. |
| `:checked` | **a checkbox or radio is on.** Resolved during the build from the input's live state, rather than supplied by the shell as `:hover` and `:active` are. |
| `:current` | **this link names the path you are on.** Matches an element whose `to` is the route you are currently on. It is the nav highlight, without a signal to track it. |
| `:enter-from` | **the frame an element enters from.** Under `r-transition`: the style the element holds for exactly one frame as it arrives, and animates away from. The *hidden* end of the animation goes here. |
| `:leave-to` | **the state an element leaves to.** Under `r-transition`: the style the element animates towards while it is held on screen on its way out. `position: absolute` here takes it out of flow, so the rest of a list closes up under it rather than waiting. |
| `:disabled` | **an input or button that is switched off.** Matches a `<input>` or `<button>` with `disabled` (or a truthy `:disabled`). Rux draws no default look for it, so this is where the dimming goes. |
| `:enabled` | **an input or button that is not disabled.** Form controls only: a plain box is neither enabled nor disabled, as in CSS. |
| `:valid` | **an input whose value passes its checks.** Matched from the start, as in CSS. A disabled or readonly input is neither valid nor invalid. |
| `:invalid` | **an input whose value fails a check.** `required`, `minlength`, `pattern`, a number's `min`/`max`, or the shape `inputmode="email"` or `"url"` implies. Matched from the start, so an empty required field is invalid before anyone has touched it: `:user-invalid` waits. |
| `:user-valid` | **valid, once the person has been through it.** Like `:valid`, but only after the field was changed and left, or its form's submission was tried. |
| `:user-invalid` | **invalid, once the person has been through it.** Like `:invalid`, but only after the field was changed and left, or its form's submission was tried. The one to put error styling on. |
| `:required` | **an input with `required`.** Inputs only. |
| `:optional` | **an input without `required`.** Inputs only. |
| `:first-child` | **the first of its siblings.** Counted among the elements drawn there, so a row an `r-if` leaves out is not counted. |
| `:last-child` | **the last of its siblings.** The siblings are counted before they are built: each `r-for` row, and the branch each `r-if` chain takes. A row animating out is not counted. |
| `:only-child` | **the one element in its parent.** Counted as `:last-child` is. |
| `:nth-child` | **`:nth-child(an+b)`: by its place among its siblings.** Counted from 1: `odd`, `even`, `3`, `2n+1`, `-n+3`. The `of S` form is not read yet. |
| `:nth-last-child` | **`:nth-last-child(an+b)`: counted from the end.** As `:nth-child()`, from the last sibling back: `:nth-last-child(-n+2)` is the last two. |
| `:not` | **`:not(a, b)`: matches none of these.** Takes compound selectors (`.done`, `button:disabled`), separated by commas, and counts as specific as the most specific of them. A combinator inside (`:not(.a .b)`) is not read yet, and the rule never matches. |
| `:is` | **`:is(a, b)`: matches any of these.** Takes full selectors, combinators included (`.x:is(.group:hover *)`), and counts as specific as the most specific of them. A forgiving list, as in CSS: an argument that does not parse is dropped, not the whole rule. |
| `:where` | **`:where(a, b)`: as `:is()`, with no weight.** Matches what `:is()` matches and adds nothing to specificity, so any later rule overrides it. The usual way a reset or a library keeps out of the author's way. |
| `:dir` | **the element's text direction.** `:dir(rtl)` or `:dir(ltr)`: what the `dir` attribute says, on the element or its nearest ancestor that has one, and `ltr` where none does. Tailwind's `rtl:` and `ltr:` are written with it. `dir="auto"` counts as saying nothing. |
| `:root` | **the top element of the app.** The screen's own element, so `:root { --accent: #89b4fa; }` sets a variable for everything under it: the place for an app's colours and sizes. |

## Known, and not honored yet

Real CSS an author reaches for, which the runtime parses, ignores and reports as a pending feature rather than a typo:

`float`, `clear`, `order`, `writing-mode`, `hyphens`, `hyphenate-character`, `perspective`, `perspective-origin`, `column-span`.
